slot.brief: At same temperature compare rms speeds of two gases of given molar masses; extend to find temperature at which a lighter gas matches rms speed of a heavier one.

stem: The molar masses of helium and oxygen are $4$ g mol$^{-1}$ and $32$ g mol$^{-1}$, respectively. At what temperature will helium have the same rms speed as oxygen at $300$ K?

verdicts.working: Set the rms-speed expressions equal: T_He/4 = 300/32, so T_He = 37.5 K.

working:
For equal rms speeds, $\dfrac{T_{\text{He}}}{M_{\text{He}}}=\dfrac{T_{\text{O}_2}}{M_{\text{O}_2}}$.
$T_{\text{He}}=300\times\dfrac{4}{32}=37.5$ K.

Independent check: Set the rms-speed expressions equal: T_He/4 = 300/32, so T_He = 37.5 K.
solution:
Since $v_{\text{rms}}=\sqrt{3RT/M}$, equal rms speeds require equal $T/M$.
$$\frac{T_{\text{He}}}{4}=\frac{300}{32}\quad\Rightarrow\quad T_{\text{He}}=37.5\text{ K}$$
